thread:
Maya (PM): quick sync — need to lock PRD acceptance for the new embeddings "Predictable Tail" work. customers A + B asked for clear latency contracts and a documented fallback path. i sketched acceptance checks below, pls comment :eyes:
Sanjay (SRE): TL;DR we should separate two things: 1) operational SLOs (p95/p99 latency, error budget) and 2) behavioral acceptance (what happens when SLOs are violated).
Olivia (Eng): agreed. proposed rollout: canary -> 10% weighted -> 50% -> 100%, with automated rollback on error budget burn > 30% in 1h. is that what you had in mind @Maya?
Maya (PM): yes, canary plan sounds right. need explicit acceptance criteria in the PRD for each rollout step. include a short test plan for customer-facing regressions.
Ravi (ML): a couple of ML-specific concerns: when we fallback (smaller model / quantized variant), we need a measurable quality threshold. for embeddings, measure mean cosine similarity on our benchmark set. i'd propose: mean cosine drop <= 0.04 and 95th percentile drop <= 0.08.
QA: i'll add those to the test matrix. also need edge cases: cold cache after redeploy, long-tail sequence inputs, and request spikes from batch jobs. we should have synthetic traffic tests for those.
Sanjay (SRE): operational SLO proposal: availability 99.95% (per-month), p95 latency <= 200ms, p99 <= 450ms for typical 1-2k token inference. error budget burn window: 30d. also define a short-circuit timeout at 1s to avoid cascading queues.
Maya (PM): good. can we capture fallback strategies in the PRD as ordered list: 1) prefix/KV cache lookup 2) model variant (quantized/condensed) 3) proxy cached response (stale-if-error) 4) soft failure with user-facing message?
Sanjay (SRE): yep. add operational constraints: when switching to fallback model, ensure KV cache compatibility and label metrics so we can split traffic measurements by variant. also add a circuit-breaker on error-rate > 5% over 5m.
Olivia (Eng): note on testing: add an integration test that asserts degradations are within thresholds and that telemetry (tagged by variant) is emitted. here's a quick config snippet we can put in the PRD for clarity:
```
acceptance:
  slo:
    availability: "99.95%"
    latency_p95_ms: "200"
    latency_p99_ms: "450"
  degrade_policy:
    order:
      - "cache_lookup"
      - "fallback_model:quantized-v2"
      - "serve_cached_stale"
      - "soft_fail_message"
  quality_thresholds:
    mean_cosine_drop: "0.04"
    p95_cosine_drop: "0.08"
```
Ravi (ML): that looks good. add a note: any fallback model must have a verified memory/KV layout match or migration plan. otherwise we risk bad cache hits.
QA: i'll add e2e scenarios: simulated region outage, spike + cache miss, model oom. we should also validate observability for each scenario (alerts, graphs, traces).
Maya (PM): next actions: Olivia to write the PRD acceptance section with the config snippet + rollout checklist. SRE to draft guardrails for deployment (circuit-breaker thresholds, rollback triggers). ML to define evaluation harness and benchmark set. QA to draft test cases. i'll consolidate and circulate for stakeholder review by EOD Friday. :+1:
DeployBot: deployment checklist all green for canary infra changes (no blockers).
Sanjay (SRE): one more thing — include a clear customer-facing SLA paragraph in the PRD that maps SLOs to compensation/commitment language for sales/legal to review. don't leave fuzzy wording.
Maya (PM): noted. thanks all — comments inline on the PRD draft when i post it.
Olivia (Eng): adding a couple of inline TODOs in the PRD: 1) telemetry tag names 2) runbook steps for graceful degrade 3) regression thresholds for embeddings.
Ravi (ML): i'll attach the benchmark CSV and evaluation script in the PRD draft.
QA: i'll schedule a short test-run session next Wed to run the synthetic scenarios.
Maya (PM): perfect. wrapping up — we have the acceptance bullets and next owners. will post the PRD link shortly. :rocket:
